  <sub>`external-locations-and-storage-credentials` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-11 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/external-locations-and-storage-credentials.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-storage/) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-storage/storage-credentials) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-storage/external-locations) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-storage/manage-external-locations) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-storage/managed-storage) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-services/service-credentials) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-services/use-service-credentials) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-create-location) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-storage/s3/s3-external-location-manual) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/access-control/privileges-reference) <sub>2026-09-11</sub></sub>
- **[Governed tags](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/governed-tags/)** — Governed tags are account-level tag keys with a fixed list of allowed values and their own assign permission, which is what makes them safe to write access policies against.  
  <sub>`governed-tags` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/governed-tags.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/governed-tags/) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/governed-tags/manage-governed-tags) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/governed-tags/manage-permissions) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/governed-tags/automate-tag-assignment) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/database-objects/tags) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-create-governed-tag) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-set-tag) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/information-schema/column_tags) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/governed-tags) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/) <sub>2026-09-12</sub></sub>
- **[Lakehouse Federation](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/lakehouse-federation/)** — Query MySQL, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, Glue and others from Unity Catalog without moving the data, through connections and foreign catalogs, read-only and with pushdown.  
  <sub>`lakehouse-federation` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-11 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/lakehouse-federation.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/query-federation/) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/query-federation/database-federation) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/query-federation/catalog-federation) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/functions/remote_query) <sub>2026-09-11</sub></sub>
- **[Managed and external tables](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/managed-vs-external-tables/)** — In a managed table Unity Catalog governs both metadata and files and deletes them on DROP; in an external table it governs only the metadata, and the files stay in the path you specified with LOCATION.  
  <sub>`managed-vs-external-tables` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/managed-vs-external-tables.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/managed) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/external) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/convert-to-managed) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-alter-table) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Managed and external volumes](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/volumes-managed-vs-external/)** — A managed volume lives in the schema's managed storage and its files are purged after a 7-day window when dropped; an external volume registers a path you own and leaves the files behind.  
  <sub>`volumes-managed-vs-external` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/volumes-managed-vs-external.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/volumes/) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/volumes/privileges) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/volumes/paths) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-volumes) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-create-volume) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-drop-volume) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/volumes/my-files) <sub>2026-09-12</sub></sub>
- **[Privileges: GRANT, REVOKE, and DENY](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/privileges-grant-revoke/)** — Unity Catalog privileges are granted to users, groups and service principals and inherit from the catalog down. USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA are the entry door.  
  <sub>`privileges-grant-revoke` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/privileges-grant-revoke.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/privileges) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/security-grant) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/security-deny) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Row filters and column masks](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/row-filters-column-masks/)** — A row filter is a SQL UDF deciding which rows a user sees; a column mask transforms a value. Both attach with ALTER TABLE and tell groups apart with is_account_group_member.  
  <sub>`row-filters-column-masks` · advanced · updated 2026-09-11 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/row-filters-column-masks.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/row-and-column-filters) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-row-filter) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-column-mask) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[System tables](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/system-tables/)** — The system catalog holds read-only tables that record cost, job runs, audit events, lineage, compute and query history for every workspace in a cloud region.  
  <sub>`system-tables` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-11 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/system-tables.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/billing) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/pricing) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/jobs) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/audit-logs) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/lineage) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/compute) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/query-history) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/warehouse-events) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/cli/reference/system-schemas-commands) <sub>2026-09-11</sub></sub>
- **[The information schema](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/information-schema/)** — The SQL standard metadata views in every Unity Catalog catalog, filtered by what you are allowed to see, and the fastest way to answer questions about your own data estate.  
  <sub>`information-schema` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/information-schema.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-information-schema) <sub>2026-09-12</sub></sub>
- **[The metastore and how a workspace gets Unity Catalog](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/uc-metastore-and-setup/)** — One metastore per cloud region holds the catalogs; the account console attaches it to workspaces; workspaces created after 8 November 2023 arrive already enabled with their own workspace catalog.  
  <sub>`uc-metastore-and-setup` · beginner · updated 2026-09-11 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/uc-metastore-and-setup.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/setup-uc/) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/enable-workspaces) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-metastore) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/catalogs/default) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-storage/managed-storage) <sub>2026-09-11</sub></sub>
- **[Unity Catalog, the governance layer](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/unity-catalog-overview/)** — Unity Catalog is the central metastore of Databricks. Three-level namespace, securable objects, credentials to storage, lineage and audit shared by every workspace in a region.  
  <sub>`unity-catalog-overview` · beginner · updated 2026-09-11 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/unity-catalog-overview.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/hive-metastore) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-storage/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Workspace-catalog binding](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/catalog-workspace-binding/)** — Every catalog in a metastore is reachable from every attached workspace until you bind it. Binding restricts a catalog to named workspaces, optionally read-only, and overrides individual grants.  
  <sub>`catalog-workspace-binding` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/catalog/catalog-workspace-binding.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/access-control/workspace-catalog-binding) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/catalogs/) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/best-practices) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-storage/manage-external-locations) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/connect/unity-catalog/cloud-storage/manage-storage-credentials) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-alter-catalog) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/information-schema/catalogs) <sub>2026-09-12</sub></sub>

### Jobs & Pipelines

- **[Change data capture with AUTO CDC](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/pipelines-auto-cdc/)** — AUTO CDC and AUTO CDC FROM SNAPSHOT apply a change feed or a sequence of snapshots to a streaming table as SCD Type 1 or Type 2, handling out-of-order events for you.  
  <sub>`pipelines-auto-cdc` · advanced · updated 2026-09-11 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/jobs-pipelines/pipelines-auto-cdc.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/cdc) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/ldp-sql-ref-apply-changes-into) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-engineering/what-is-cdc) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/ldp-python-ref-apply-changes) <sub>2026-09-11</sub></sub>
- **[Choosing SQL or Python for a pipeline](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/pipelines-sql-vs-python/)** — Both pipeline interfaces build the same dataflow graph, so most of the choice is taste. The asymmetries are few and they all run one way: Python covers the whole feature set, SQL does not.  
  <sub>`pipelines-sql-vs-python` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/jobs-pipelines/pipelines-sql-vs-python.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/sql-vs-python) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/sql-dev) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/python-dev) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/dbsql/dbsql-for-ldp) <sub>2026-09-12</sub></sub>
- **[Concurrent runs, queueing, and the limits behind them](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/jobs-queue-and-concurrency/)** — max_concurrent_runs defaults to 1 and caps at 1000. With queueing on, a run that hits one of three limits waits up to 48 hours instead of being skipped. The exact numbers are what the exam asks about.  
  <sub>`jobs-queue-and-concurrency` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/jobs-pipelines/jobs-queue-and-concurrency.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/configure-job) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/limits) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/jobs/create) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/jobs/getrun) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/continuous) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/jobs) <sub>2026-09-12</sub></sub>
- **[Continuous jobs](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/jobs-continuous/)** — A continuous job keeps exactly one run alive, restarting it in under a minute when it ends and backing off exponentially when it keeps failing. On serverless, only bounded triggers work.  
  <sub>`jobs-continuous` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/jobs-pipelines/jobs-continuous.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/continuous) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/jobs/create) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/serverless/streaming) <sub>2026-09-12</sub></sub>
- **[Control flow: retries, if/else, for each, run job](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/jobs-control-flow/)** — Per-task retries and timeouts, If/else tasks for conditional branches, For each for loops, and Run job for composing jobs: the control logic lives in the graph, not in the code.  
  <sub>`jobs-control-flow` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/jobs-pipelines/jobs-control-flow.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/conditional-tasks) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/if-else) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/for-each) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/configure-task) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/run-job) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/jobs/create) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Data quality: expectations and constraints](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/pipelines-expectations/)** — Declarative pipeline expectations (warn, drop, fail) and Delta NOT NULL and CHECK constraints. Where each one is declared, what happens on a violation, and how to read the metrics in the event log.  
  <sub>`pipelines-expectations` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-11 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/jobs-pipelines/pipelines-expectations.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/expectations) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/constraints) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/python-ref) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Job and task parameters, dynamic values, and task values](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/jobs-parameters/)** — Job parameters apply to every task, task parameters to just one; dynamic values like {{job.start_time.iso_date}} carry context; task values pass results from one task to another.  
  <sub>`jobs-parameters` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/jobs-pipelines/jobs-parameters.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/job-parameters) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/parameter-use) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/dynamic-value-references) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/task-values) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Lakeflow Jobs, what a job is](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/jobs-overview/)** — A job is the unit of orchestration in Databricks, a graph of tasks that runs on a compute of your choice, with triggers, parameters, and notifications.  
  <sub>`jobs-overview` · beginner · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/jobs-pipelines/jobs-overview.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/configure-task) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Lakeflow pipelines](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/pipelines-overview/)** — A declarative pipeline describes streaming tables and materialized views in SQL or Python; the engine works out the graph, ordering and incremental updates. Formerly Delta Live Tables.  
  <sub>`pipelines-overview` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-11 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/jobs-pipelines/pipelines-overview.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/concepts/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/python-ref) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/python-dev) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/sql-dev) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/updates) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/configure-pipeline) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/monitor-event-logs) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2025/june) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Repair runs, retries, and notifications](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/jobs-repair-runs/)** — A repair reruns only the failed tasks and their downstream tasks within the same run; notifications via email or system destinations, duration-based health rules, and queueing round out error handling.  
  <sub>`jobs-repair-runs` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/jobs-pipelines/jobs-repair-runs.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/repair-job-failures) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/notifications) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/configure-job) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/api/workspace/jobs/repairrun) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Serverless compute for jobs](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/jobs-serverless/)** — Serverless is the default compute for most Lakeflow Jobs tasks. Which task types take it, how environments and performance modes are declared, and when a job cluster still wins.  
  <sub>`jobs-serverless` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-11 · [source](content/concepts/02-workspace/jobs-pipelines/jobs-serverless.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/run-serverless-jobs) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/compute) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/serverless/) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/serverless/limitations) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/serverless/best-practices) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/serverless/dependencies) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/bundles/examples) <sub>2026-09-11</sub></sub>
- **[Sinks: writing out of a pipeline](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/pipelines-sinks/)** — A sink lets a pipeline flow write somewhere that is not a pipeline-managed table, such as a Kafka topic or an external Delta table. Declared with create_sink, fed by an append flow, Python only.

Time-based vs. data-driven is a favorite exam question.

## Data Engineering

### Runs

- **[Monitoring runs: states, run history, trends](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/runs-monitoring/)** — The Runs page and a job's run history show states, durations, and the task graph. Comparing a run against the historical baseline is the first step in telling whether a job is getting worse.

### Data Ingestion

- **[Auto Loader](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/auto-loader/)** — Auto Loader is the cloudFiles streaming source that incrementally loads new files from object storage, with schema inference, schema evolution and a _rescued_data column.  
  <sub>`auto-loader` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/data-ingestion/auto-loader.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/auto-loader/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/auto-loader/schema) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/auto-loader/file-notification-mode) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/auto-loader/production) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[COPY INTO](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/copy-into/)** — COPY INTO is the idempotent SQL command that loads files from object storage into a Delta table, remembering what it already loaded and running from a SQL warehouse.  
  <sub>`copy-into` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/data-ingestion/copy-into.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/copy-into/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/delta-copy-into) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>

- **[Ingestion patterns: batch, streaming, incremental](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/ingestion-patterns/)** — Batch, streaming and incremental are the three ways into the lakehouse, served by UI uploads, standard connectors and Lakeflow Connect. Choosing between them is an exam question.  
  <sub>`ingestion-patterns` · beginner · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/data-ingestion/ingestion-patterns.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ingestion/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ingestion/file-upload/upload-data) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>

  <sub>`lakeflow-connect` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/data-ingestion/lakeflow-connect.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ingestion/lakeflow-connect/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ingestion/lakeflow-connect/saas-overview) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ingestion/lakeflow-connect/sql-server-overview) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ingestion/lakeflow-connect/salesforce) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>

### Delta Lake

- **[Change Data Feed](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/change-data-feed/)** — Change Data Feed records every row-level insert, update, and delete on a Delta table so downstream jobs can propagate just the change, not the whole table.  
  <sub>`change-data-feed` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-10 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/delta-lake/change-data-feed.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/delta-change-data-feed) <sub>2026-09-10</sub></sub>
- **[Deletion vectors](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/deletion-vectors/)** — Deletion vectors record deleted and updated rows in metadata instead of rewriting whole Parquet files, and every reader applies them at scan time to work out which rows still count.  
  <sub>`deletion-vectors` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/delta-lake/deletion-vectors.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/features/deletion-vectors) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/optimizations/isolation/row-level-concurrency) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/delta-reorg-table) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/vacuum) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/workspace-settings/deletion-vectors) <sub>2026-09-12</sub></sub>
- **[Delta Lake, the lakehouse table format](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/delta-lake-overview/)** — Delta Lake is Parquet plus a transaction log. The log provides ACID transactions, time travel, schema enforcement, and a history you can inspect with DESCRIBE HISTORY.  
  <sub>`delta-lake-overview` · beginner · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/delta-lake/delta-lake-overview.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/history) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/update-schema) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Gold objects: tables, views, materialized views, streaming tables](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/gold-layer-objects/)** — The four objects you use to expose the gold layer in Unity Catalog. What they store, how they refresh, what they cost, and when to pick one over another.  
  <sub>`gold-layer-objects` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/delta-lake/gold-layer-objects.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/views/) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/views/materialized) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dlt/streaming-tables) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-create-streaming-table) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Iceberg on Databricks](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/iceberg-interoperability/)** — Managed Iceberg tables, foreign Iceberg tables, Iceberg reads on Delta, and the REST catalog that lets an engine outside Databricks read the same rows.  
  <sub>`iceberg-interoperability` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/delta-lake/iceberg-interoperability.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/iceberg/) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/external-access/iceberg) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/uniform) <sub>2026-09-12</sub></sub>
- **[Liquid clustering](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/liquid-clustering/)** — Liquid Clustering replaces partitioning and Z-ORDER with mutable clustering keys and incremental OPTIMIZE; predictive optimization runs OPTIMIZE, VACUUM, and statistics on its own on managed tables.  
  <sub>`liquid-clustering` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/delta-lake/liquid-clustering.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/clustering) <sub>2026-09-09</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/optimizations/predictive-optimization) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[Medallion architecture: bronze, silver, gold](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/medallion-architecture/)** — Three layers of Delta tables with increasing quality. Bronze keeps the raw data, silver cleans and types it, gold aggregates it for the business.  
  <sub>`medallion-architecture` · beginner · updated 2026-09-09 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/delta-lake/medallion-architecture.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/lakehouse/medallion) <sub>2026-09-09</sub></sub>
- **[OPTIMIZE, VACUUM, and file layout](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/delta-optimize-vacuum/)** — OPTIMIZE compacts small files, VACUUM removes ones no version needs after a 7-day default retention, and predictive optimization now runs both for you.  
  <sub>`delta-optimize-vacuum` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-10 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/delta-lake/delta-optimize-vacuum.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/optimize) <sub>2026-09-10</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/vacuum) <sub>2026-09-10</sub></sub>

  <sub>`data-layout-partitioning-zorder` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/delta-lake/data-layout-partitioning-zorder.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/clustering) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/partitions) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/tune-file-size) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/data-skipping) <sub>2026-09-12</sub></sub>

  <sub>`predictive-optimization` · intermediate · updated 2026-09-12 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/delta-lake/predictive-optimization.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/optimizations/predictive-optimization) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/predictive-optimization) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/data-skipping) <sub>2026-09-12</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/tune-file-size) <sub>2026-09-12</sub></sub>

### Streaming

- **[Arbitrary sinks with foreachBatch](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/foreachbatch/)** — foreachBatch hands each micro-batch to your own function as a batch DataFrame. It guarantees at-least-once, so exactly-once is something you build on batchId.  
  <sub>`foreachbatch` · advanced · updated 2026-09-11 · [source](content/concepts/04-data-engineering/streaming/foreachbatch.md) · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/structured-streaming/foreach) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/structured-streaming/delta-lake) <sub>2026-09-11</sub> · [docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/structured-streaming/real-time/reference) <sub>2026-09-11</sub></sub>
- **[Reading and writing Apache Kafka](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/kafka-streaming/)** — The kafka format as a Structured Streaming source and sink: record schema, offsets, checkpoints, authentication, and the end-to-end Kafka to Delta pattern.

## AI & Machine Learning

### Playground

### Agents

- **[Agent Bricks: Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent](https://lakenaut.dev/concepts/agent-bricks/)** — Two declarative agent builders: Knowledge Assistant answers questions over your documents with citations, and Supervisor Agent routes a request across up to 50 subagents and tools.

## Learning paths

- **[SQL & Python Foundations](https://lakenaut.dev/paths/foundations/)** — The SQL and PySpark you need before any other path: the Spark dialect, types, joins, windows, MERGE, and the DataFrame API as it differs from pandas. <sub>4 stages</sub>
- **[Lakehouse Foundations](https://lakenaut.dev/paths/lakehouse-foundations/)** — How the Databricks platform is put together: control plane and compute, Delta Lake as the storage format, Unity Catalog as the governance layer, and the medallion pattern everything else builds on. <sub>4 stages</sub>
- **[Data Engineering](https://lakenaut.dev/paths/data-engineering/)** — Build production pipelines: ingest with Auto Loader, COPY INTO and Lakeflow Connect, transform with PySpark and SQL, orchestrate with Lakeflow Jobs, and ship it with bundles. <sub>6 stages</sub>
- **[Governance & Security](https://lakenaut.dev/paths/governance-security/)** — Unity Catalog end to end: the three-level namespace, managed and external tables, privileges, row filters, column masks and attribute-based policies. <sub>4 stages</sub>
- **[Platform & Administration](https://lakenaut.dev/paths/platform-administration/)** — Choose the right compute, read the Spark UI, tune the handful of settings that matter, and diagnose clusters that will not start or run out of memory. <sub>4 stages</sub>
- **[SQL & Analytics](https://lakenaut.dev/paths/sql-analytics/)** — Query the lakehouse from the SQL editor, model gold tables and views for BI, and understand what a SQL warehouse costs. <sub>3 stages</sub>
- **[Machine Learning](https://lakenaut.dev/paths/machine-learning/)** — Track experiments with MLflow, build features, register models in Unity Catalog and serve them behind an endpoint. <sub>3 stages</sub>
- **[Generative AI](https://lakenaut.dev/paths/generative-ai/)** — Foundation models on Databricks, vector search for retrieval, agents built with Agent Bricks and the Agent Framework, and how to evaluate them. <sub>4 stages</sub>
